paper_title: MADLLM Multivariate Anomaly Detection via Pre-trained LLMs
caption: figures/ablation_title.pdf
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the F1 Score (%) of the MADLLM model and its ablated variants across six different datasets—SMD, PSM, SWaT, SMAP, MSL, and WADI—showing the impact of removing specific components: feature embedding, prompt pool, and skip embedding. The vertical axis represents F1 Score ranging from 60% to 100% in increments of 10, while the horizontal axis lists the datasets in the specified order. Each dataset has four grouped bars, colored green (MADLLM), purple (MADLLM w/o feature embedding), blue (MADLLM w/o prompt pool), and orange (MADLLM w/o skip embedding), as indicated by the legend below the chart. On SMD, all variants perform similarly, with scores around 90–93%. On PSM, the full MADLLM achieves the highest score (~97%), while removing the prompt pool causes a noticeable drop to ~77%. For SWaT, MADLLM scores ~91%, and removing skip embedding reduces performance to ~85%. On SMAP, the full model scores ~93%, while removing skip embedding drops performance to ~67%. For MSL, MADLLM scores ~87%, and removing the prompt pool reduces it to ~69%. On WADI, the full model scores ~74%, while removing feature embedding causes the largest drop to ~63%. Overall, the full MADLLM consistently outperforms or matches its ablated variants, with the prompt pool and feature embedding showing particularly strong contributions on certain datasets.
